## Subject- Functioning of ODD (Obstruction and Derailment Detection) device and Marking of saloon door numbers in RS-10 trains
## (a) OTM RS-10 Version 1.0 Part-A Chapter-5, Para-5.15 shall be added as below:
## 5.15 Overview of ODD (Obstruction and Derailment Detection) device:

## 5.15 Overview of ODD (Obstruction and Derailment Detection) device:

Obstruction  and  Derailment  Detection  Device  (ODD)  is  a  device that can detect  any obstacle lying on the track that may hit the underframe of the train and also detects derailment of the train.
Its main function is to apply emergency brake under emergency circumstances such as obstacle  crash  or  derailment  and  create  a  safe  vehicle  operation  by  stopping  the vehicle. It is  installed  in  front  at  the  bottom  of  the  DM  car  front  bogie. It  consists  of  a detection  bar  that  is  connected  to  the  sensing  device  and  configured  spring  that  is located at both ends.
The sensors will detect the horizontal and vertical movement of the detection bar. If there is an obstacle, the detection bar is pushed in horizontal direction at a defined rotation angle and obstruction is sensed by the sensor located in the sensor box which gives input to  apply  Emergency  Brake  and  send  status  to  TCMS.  In  the  case  of  derailment,  the detection bar is moved in vertical direction and derailment is sensed by the sensor, which gives input to apply Emergency Brake and send status to TCMS.
[Obstacle and Derailment Detection Device]
## 5.15.1 Functioning of ODD:

## 5.15.1 Functioning of ODD:

Whenever obstacle or derailment is sensed by the ODD, emergency brake shall be applied in train automatically. In non-UTO modes, following event shall pop-up on the TCMS that has to be acknowledged by RA/ETO and in UTO mode, same events shall be relayed to OCC. Further below given procedure shall be followed.

## 5.15.1 Functioning of ODD:

Event Code 14022- Obstacle Detection RA/ETO can check the status on TCMS will  be  shown  in  RED colour.
Event Code  14023- Derailment Detection RA/ETO can check the status on TCMS Current Event Log for derailment detection fault.

## 6.1.2 :    3-digit Saloon door numbering in trains to facilitate passengers in UTO lines-

In  case of non-operational saloon door/s or PSD due to any failure, RA/ETO/OCC shall make  manual  announcement  for  information  of  passengers  inside  train.  For  ease  of identification  of  faulty/non-operational  door  by  passengers  as  well  as  RA/ETO/OCC, 3-digit  Door  Numbering  Stickers  are  available  on  both  sides  (internal)  at  each  saloon door, driving area of the train and OCC. RA/ETO/OCC shall use the below mentioned nomenclature, for identification of doors, while making manual announcements inside the trains.

## 6.1.2 :    3-digit Saloon door numbering in trains to facilitate passengers in UTO lines-

3-digit Door Numbering sticker available on both sides of Saloon Door

1.2.3 Train  Start  Up: On  pressing  'Aux  On'  button  for  2  seconds, initialization  of  trains starts.  Train  prepares  itself for operation.  The  sequence  of events  is  as  under:

## Introduction

'Aux-On/PANTO  UP'  button  is  pressed. i.
Start-up  Relay  energizes. ii.
If  MR  pressure  is  less  than  6  bars,  Auxiliary  Compressor  Motor  (ACM)  starts utilizing Battery Supply & builds pressure for raising Pantograph. If  MR pressure is more  than 6 bars, then pantograph  will utilize the existing  MR pressure  andACM  will  not  be  operated. ili.
Pantograph starts rising and is detected as 'Raised' by TCMS when 'Pantograph Pressure Switch' reading becomes at least 3.9 bars in pantograph  pneumatic  circuit. iv.
When  Pantographs  are  detected  raised  &  Line  voltage  is  detected in  OHE, VCB  closes & Line voltage is available for train equipment  through Main Transformer. V.
If the conditions for Main Compressor  operation are satisfied then Main Compressor  Motor  starts  and  begins  building  Main  Reservoir  (MR)  pressure.
ACM  stops  when  Main  Compressor  Motor starts.
As  pneumatic  pressure  builds  up,  Emergency  brake  start  taking  over  Parking Brake. At MR Pressure 5.2 Bar Parking Brakes completely release & Emergency  Brakes  remain  applied  on  Train.

## Introduction

When  MR  pressure  rises  above  7.0  Bar, EB  releases  and Holding  brakes  & Service  brakes  remain  applied  on  train  in  case  any  cab  is  energized.

## Introduction

_ Holding  Brakes  will  remain  applied  till  sufficient  Motoring  command  is  initiated from  TBC.
1.3. Working  of  Master  Controller  Panel-  The  various  parts  of  Master  Controller  Panel &  their  working are  as  under:
1.3.1 MASCON Key and Key Switch: For energizing a cab, a Master Controller (MASCON)  key  is  inserted  in  the  Master  Controller  Key  switch.  Key  is  then  rotated by  90  degree  in  anti-clockwise  direction.  The  other  control  levers  of  Master  Control Panels  can  be  now  operated  as  per a  mechanical  interlocking.
At  'ON'  position  the  MASCON  key  is  physically  retained  within  the  Key  Switch.  The MASCON  key  can  only  be  removed  when  the  Mode  Selector  is  at  'OFF'  or  'AUTO' Position  and  Key  Switch  is  at'OFF'  position.
1.3.2 Mode  Selector  (MS):  It  has  6  positions  and  is  used  to  select  the  mode  of  driving.

1.3.4 Dead  Man  Safety  Device  (DSD):  lt  is  designed  to  ensure  that  if  Train  Operator  is incapacitated  due  to  any  reason,  train  comes  to  a  halt  by  application  of  Emergency Brake. It  is  incorporated  in  the  Traction  Brake  Controller  handle.  To  activate  DSD, the  TBC handle must be rotated in clockwise direction. If  TBC  grab handle is released  when  it  is  at  Motoring, Coasting  or  Braking,  the  DSD is  deactivated  and irrevocable  Emergency  Brake  is  applied.

## 1.4.7 Stopping  a  Train:

## 1.4.7 Stopping  a  Train:

Service  Brake:  Train  can be  stopped normally  by  initiating  braking  command using  TBC.  When  TBC  is  put  within  the  range  'MIN-MAX  BRAKING'  service brakes  are  applied  in  the  train. In  this  type  of  braking,  brakes  are  controlled  by Brake  Computer  i.e.  Brake  Electronic  Control  Unit  (BECU)  which  is  available  in each  bogie.  It  includes  both  regenerative  and  electro-pneumatic  braking.

## 1.4.7 Stopping  a  Train:

Emergency  Brake (EB): In Emergency  situation train can be stopped by applying Emergency  brakes. EB can be applied using  TBC by putting it at position  'EM'.  Itcan  be  also  applied  by  pressing  EBPE  push  button  available  on Operating  panel  |  &  II  of  front  cab  or  from  EBPB  of  Operating  Panel | & Il  from rear  cab. EB  is  also  applied if  DSD  (Daad  man  Safety  Device)  is  in  released position  and  DSD  bypass  switch  is  at  'NORMAL'  position.  This  kind  of  braking has  maximum  braking  effort. It  does  not  have  any  intervention  of  BECU  and  is applied  by  disruption  of  Emergency  Brake  Loop'  in  Active  Cab.
iii, BP-Back  up  Brake  (DBV): Brakes  can  also  be  applied  by  putting  Driver  Brake Valve  (DBV)  at  Position-V  in  active/last  active  cab.  Itis  a  fully  pneumatic  braking system.  In  this kind  of  braking, brake  signal  transmission is  pneumatic  due  to which  it  is  slower  in  application  as  compared  to  Service  &  Emergency  brake. The braking effort by BP Back Up brake is also variable, however  highest braking  effort  is  equivalent to Emergency  brake.
## 1.4.8 Braking  using  'Driver  Brake  Valve'  (DBV):

## 1.4.8 Braking  using  'Driver  Brake  Valve'  (DBV):

DBV  braking  is  normally  used  during  rescue  operations  or  in  case  of  failure  of  both Service  Brake  and  Emergency  Brake.  DBV  is  used  to  reduce  the  pressure  of  Brake Pipe  (BP)  from  the  normal  level i.e. 5 Bar. This, in turn, triggers  the  application  of brakes  by  allowing  pneumatic  pressure  from  Supply  Reservoir  to  Brake  Cylinder. The  braking  strength is directly proportional  to  the reduction in the BP  pressure. However, when BP pressure drops < 3.5 bars, Emergency  Brake Loop is deenergized  and  irrevocable  Emergency  brake  is  triggered.

## Operation  of Wipers6.6

There  are  two  wiper  switches to  control  Left  &  Right wiper  functions.  The  switches are  placed  on Operating  Panel  II on left  side of  the  operator  desk. It  has  five positions:
Position  'OFF'-  The  wipers  shall  remain  OFF  at  this  position.
Position 'LONG'The  wipers shall move in long time difference. If  wiper switch  is  pressed,  water  is  released  at  this  position.
Position  'SHORTThe  wipers  shall  move  in  short  time  difference. If  wiper switch  is  pressed,  water  is  released  at  this  position.
Position 'LOW'The wipers shall move in low speed. If  wiper switch is pressed, water is  released  at  this  position.
Position "HIGH'-  The  wipers shall move in High speed. If  wiper  switch is pressed, water is  released  at  this  position.
## 6.7 Functioning  of  VCB  Opening/Closing  while  negotiating  Neutral  section:

## 6.7 Functioning  of  VCB  Opening/Closing  while  negotiating  Neutral  section:

In  ATP/AUTO  mode,  VCB  opens  automatically  as Neutral section input comes  from  signaling  system  85  meters  before  Neutral  section.  If  signaling input is not available then also VCB  opens automatically due to route correctly fed in PA/PIS system works as a backup mode for VCB opening/closing.
In degraded mode, signaling input is not available so for automatic operation  of  VCB  in Neutral  section, route  must  be  correctly  fed in  PA/PIS system manually through TCMS or MOU. If due to any reason, correct/manual  route  cannot  be  fed  then  automatic  operation  of  VCB will not be possible In Neutral section and  VCB  open/close is to be manually  done  by  Train  Operator  through  VCB  open/close  push  buttons  by following  VCB  open/close  boards  available  in  Neutral  section.
Note-  While negotiating  the  neutral section,  Train  Operator  must  observe  opening  and closing of  VCB from available indications and inform OCC  if  any  abnormality is noticed.

¢ AUTO  mode-  It  is  the  primary  mode  for  passenger  announcements  in  the  train. Route  is  automatically  configured  using  VATC  signals  when  train  receives  valid ID  and  announcements  are  played  automatically.

This  system  is  based  on  saloon  door  opening/closing sequence  and  distance  covered by train.

Cut  out  cocks are basically  provided to isolate equipment  for  the purpose of maintenance. However, some  of  the Cocks  also  have  operational importance e.g.  BIC,  EPIC  etc.  Based  upon  the  functioning  of  cocks  they  can  be  classified  as below:
Isolating Cock: On operating these cocks transmission of pressure is blocked.  However  it  doesn't affect  the  pressure  status  in  pipe  at  either  side of  it.
Drain  Cock: On  operating  these  cocks  transmission  of  pressure is  blocked and  the  pressure of  one  side  of  the  pipe  is  vented.

## CHAPTER  --7 RESCUE  OPERATION  CONCEPT

## CHAPTER  --7 RESCUE  OPERATION  CONCEPT

Whenever  a  train is stalled in mid-section due  to any  failure and the  same  cannot  be restored  within 15  minutes,  then  such  train  is  rescued  with  the  help  of  an  assisting  train. Based upon the position of  assisting train vis-a-vis defective train with respect  to the direction  of  travel,  rescue  operation  is  categorized  in  two  types.

## CHAPTER  --7 RESCUE  OPERATION  CONCEPT

Push  out  Operation: In this type of  rescue operation, generally  the train following  the  defective  train  is  coupled  to  the  defective  train  from  behind  and pushes  it  towards  the  existing  direction  of  travel.  However  if  the  assisting  train is coupled  from  the  front  of  the train and pushes  the defective train in the opposite  direction  it  is  also  a  push  out  operation.
N . Pull  Out  Operation: In  this  type  of  rescue  operation  generally  the  assisting train is coupled to the defective train from front and after coupling train operator  changes  cab  &  assisting train pulls defective train in the existing direction of  travel. However  if  the  following  train is  coupled  to  the  defective train  from  behind  and  pulls  it  back  in  the  direction  opposite  to  existing  direction oftravel,  itis  also  a  pull  out  operation.
Based  upon  the  availability  of  the  nearest  rescue  train,  diversion  and  siding  for  stabling defective  train,  Traffic  Controller  plans  the  type  of the  rescue  operation  to  be  used.
Coupling:  The  activity  of  connecting  two  units/trains  together  with  the  help  of  mechanical coupleris  called  the  Coupling.

7.1.3. Pneumatic  Connection:  After  trains are mechanically coupled two kinds of pneumatic  connection  take  place.
MRP  connection: A  train  line  Main  Reservoir  Pipe  going  from  head  to  the  tail of  the train is  available  to  supply  pneumatic  pressure  to  various  pneumatic equipment.  The  MRP  connection  between  two  coupled  trains  depends  upon the following.
MRP  Port  (commonly  referred  as  MR  port):  Itis  the  lower  port  as  available on  the  coupler  and  is  designed  to  stop  the  MR  pressure  from  venting  in normal situation. After two trains are mechanically coupled it is automatically opened to provide the pneumatic MRP connection between them.
Il. MRP  Cock:  This  is  a  drain  cock  and  is  available  in  DM  Car  cab  on  the  MR Pipe  under  TO  desk  and  at  the  other  end  of  DM  car  in  the  under  frame.  In T  and M  cars, MRP  cock  is  available  at  either  ends  in  the  under  frame. This  cock  is  normally  kept  open i.e.  its  handle  is  parallel  to  the  MR  pipe.

Ill. Single  Protection  Valve:  This  is  available  on  the  MR  pipe  between  MRP cock and hose. It is designed to block the pneumatic pressure transmission  through  it  if  the  hose  pipe  between  the  coupler  and  the  MR pipe is  broken.  Whenever  the hose pipe is burst  due  to  any  reason it senses  the  steep pressure  drop  and blocks  the  pressure  transmission through  it.
Since  in  normal  situation,  the  MRP  cock  &  Single  Protection  Valve  are  opened, therefore  the  success  of  MRP  connection  after  coupling  depends  upon  the MRP  port which is designed to open as soon as train is mechanically connected.
BP  Connection: Atrain  line  Brake  Pipe  going  from  head  to  the  tail  of  the  train is  available  to  transfer  the  BP  Backup  brake  signal  to  every  car  till  the  rear  end of the train. This  connection is very important  as it is the only method  for triggering  brakes  during  rescue  operation.  The  BP  connection between  two coupled  trains  depends  upon  the  following:

## 1.1 Troubleshooting  Principle:

## 1.1 Troubleshooting  Principle:

The  objective of  the  troubleshooting  of  a  train by  train operator  is  to clear  the blockage  of  mainline  due  to  the  faulty  train  causing  the  detention  of  the  healthy trains.  Following  guidelines  shall  be  followed  during  troubleshooting  of  the  train.

## 1.1 Troubleshooting  Principle:

Ifthe  train  is  stopped  in  mid-section  and  if fault  can  be  isolated/rectified  using any  cut-out  switch  viz.  DPLCOS,  BLCOS  or  SCS;  Train  operator  shall  operate the  relevant  cut-out  switch  and  proceed  to  the  next  station  as  per  procedure.
ii) If  train is  stopped  at  station  platform,  train  operator  shall try  to  rectify/isolate the  fault  as  per the  procedure given in  the  subsequent  chapters  of  this  manual.
iii) The  troubleshooting procedures  are  so  formulated  that  the  detention  of  the train  is  kept  minimal.
